propositions: Proposed deterministic clarity rules reject valid closed tickets with signed attestations, indicating unsound or over-broad applicability gates.
Section-heading requirements are disproven as hard oracles; semantic content and non-heading plan formats are valid.
Placeholder lexicon detection, per-AC proof markers, conjunction hygiene, and testing-scenario requirements are advisory signals, not validity thresholds.
Read-only analysis and operational tickets are incorrectly constrained by edit-set and file_impact requirements when they explicitly document no-edit contracts.

Five of six proposed criteria should be downgraded from hard rejections to coaching-level advisory flags; one (required nonempty sections with aliases) should be narrowed to semantic applicability rules.
Historical corpus of 574 closed tickets with plan-review attestation provides empirical disproof of phrase-based and formal-structure criteria as deterministic validity gates.
